prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Lange deutsche Komposita (language de).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Begriff" · longest unbreakable word 546px · one-line width 546px
  col 2: header "Kurzform" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 101px
  col 3: header "Erklärung" · longest unbreakable word 186px · one-line width 1091px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r0B: widths [220, 122, 377] · table 720×580px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 106, 106, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [567, 122, 1112] · table 1802×255px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 1082px
Design r1A: widths [296, 122, 301] · table 720×743px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 129, 129, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [282, 122, 315] · table 720×720px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 129, 129, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [306, 122, 291] · table 720×743px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 129, 129, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [320, 122, 277] · table 720×766px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 129, 129, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [567, 122, 400] · table 1090×534px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 106, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 370px
Design r3A: widths [306, 105, 308] · table 720×720px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 129, 129, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r2C"],"acceptable":["r3A","r2A","r2B"],"bad":[{"design":"r0B","why":"The first column is only 220px (199px text), far below the 546px longest term, so the table's key compounds are chopped into 3–4 short fragments; the row headers become hard to scan and compare."},{"design":"r0C","why":"The table is 1802px wide and overflows the 720px box by 1082px; explanation lines run to 1091px, so the reader loses row context and must scroll excessively to compare anything."},{"design":"r1A","why":"The 296px first column leaves a one-letter orphan in the longest compound ('...verordnun/g') and splits key terms awkwardly; the 5-line rows are a symptom of misallocated width."},{"design":"r1B","why":"The 282px first column produces one-letter orphans ('...gesellschaf/t', '...geset/z') in the row-identifying column, which is visually unacceptable."}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[567,600],[122,140],[340,480]],"rationale":"This table is about long compounds, so the first column is the primary object: at 567px it keeps the longest term intact, and 122px keeps the short forms on one line. r2C accepts a 370px horizontal scroll, but the Kurzform column remains visible as a row anchor when the reader scrolls to the explanation, so rows still read as units. A reader who values seeing all three columns at once may prefer r3A, while one who values the compounds as data will prefer r2C.","uncertain":"Whether 370px of horizontal scroll is acceptable in the intended publication context; whether the Kurzform column is reliably visible during scrolling; and whether breaks at German compound boundaries are acceptable without visible hyphens."}
